title: Runtime Sidecar Contract for Private Deployments (ADR)
author: Priya Nair
content:
Summary
-------
This ADR defines the runtime sidecar contract for Redwood Private deployments. The sidecar provides a portable, auditable, and minimal runtime surface that sits next to the customer's model-serving process to: 1) standardize how model artifacts and configs are delivered, 2) expose a stable inference and control API to the Redwood control plane and local clients, 3) provide required telemetry, health, and lifecycle hooks, and 4) enforce security controls (encryption, key management, and access policies).

Decision
--------
We adopt a lightweight sidecar contract for Private deployments with the following properties:
- A well-defined HTTP/JSON and gRPC inference API surface for request/response and streaming fallback, with explicit identity and tenant headers.
- A control API for lifecycle operations (activate, drain, update-config, snapshot-state).
- Standardized telemetry and health endpoints (Prometheus metrics, OpenTelemetry traces, and structured health probes).
- Configuration via signed manifests delivered by the Redwood control plane or an approved local repository.
- Mandatory mutual TLS (mTLS) between Redwood control plane components and sidecars; local client authentication uses short-lived tokens bound to tenant identity.
- Minimal local storage: ephemeral cache only; prompts and raw inputs must never be persisted unencrypted beyond configured retention windows.

Context and Motivation
----------------------
Private deployments span customer-managed networks (VPC and on-prem). We must balance:
1) operational consistency (the Redwood control plane must be able to orchestrate rollouts and collect observability)
2) customer sovereignty (customers must retain control of keys, networking, and artifact provenance)
3) security and compliance (no leakage of sensitive prompts or keys).

Existing ad-hoc sidecar implementations created fragmentation in how artifacts are delivered, how health is reported, and how failover is coordinated. This ADR reduces that fragmentation with a prescriptive, minimal contract.

Scope and Non-goals
-------------------
In scope:
- Sidecar-to-model process API and lifecycle behavior.
- Control plane to sidecar operations required for rollout and debug.
- Telemetry, tracing, and error classification conventions.

Out of scope:
- Inference model internals (kernel choices, quantization behavior) beyond metadata tags.
- Customer-specific metrics that are not part of the standard telemetry set (customers may expose additional metrics but must map standard names).

Contract: APIs and Endpoints
---------------------------
1) Inference HTTP/JSON API (primary):
- POST /v1/infer
  - Request: JSON body with fields: {"input": string|array, "model": string, "meta": object} (meta is optional, limited to 1KB).
  - Required headers: X-Redwood-Tenant (tenant id), X-Request-ID, Authorization: Bearer <short-lived-token>.
  - Response: {"id": string, "status": "ok" | "error", "outputs": array, "meta": object}.
  - Error model: consistent typed errors with fields: code (string), message (string), retriable (bool).

2) Streaming fallback (optional):
- gRPC Predict(stream) or HTTP/1.1 chunked with the same typed envelope. Streaming is optional for on-prem sidecars but must be supported for dedicated customer projects.

3) Control API (HTTP):
- POST /control/activate (body: {"manifest_id": string})
- POST /control/drain (body: {"grace_seconds": int})
- POST /control/update-config (body: signed manifest blob)
- GET /control/manifest (returns manifest metadata and SHA256)
- DELETE /control/snapshot (create/clear local state snapshot)

4) Health and telemetry:
- GET /healthz - returns HTTP 200 and JSON {"ready": true/false, "uptime_seconds": N, "model_state": "loaded" | "loading" | "error"}.
- /metrics - Prometheus exposition format with standard metric names (see Metrics section).
- OpenTelemetry collector endpoint (OTLP/gRPC) or export to local collector; traces must include request id and tenant.

5) Admin introspection (restricted):
- GET /admin/config (only accessible to control plane mTLS identity).

Control Plane Authentication and Identity
---------------------------------------
- Mutual TLS required for control plane <-> sidecar. Redwood control plane authenticates using short-lived certs tied to a deployment id.
- For local clients, sidecar accepts OAuth2-style short-lived bearer tokens minted by a tenant-specific auth service. Tokens are audience-limited and must be rotated <= 1 hour.
- Identity propagation: X-Redwood-Actor header to carry end-user or service identity for audit logs.

Telemetry, Metrics, and Tracing
------------------------------
Standard Prometheus metric names (mandatory):
- redwood_sidecar_requests_total{result="ok|error",model="<name>"}
- redwood_sidecar_request_duration_seconds_bucket (histogram)
- redwood_sidecar_kv_cache_hits_total
- redwood_sidecar_model_loads_total
- redwood_sidecar_pending_requests (gauge)

Tracing and correlation:
- All traces must include attributes: request.id, tenant.id, model.version, sidecar.id.
- Error spans must include structured tags: error.code, error.class.

SLOs and Operational Expectations
---------------------------------
Primary SLOs for sidecar behavior (Private):
- Availability: 99.95% uptime for control-plane reachable health (measured weekly).
- Latency: p95 end-to-end sidecar processing < 300ms for CPU-hosted small models (<=3B params); p95 < 150ms for GPU-backed models where hardware latency dominates.
- Error budget policy: sidecars contribute to customer's deployment error budget; sustained >0.5% 5xx over 15m triggers an alert and automatic limited rollback to previous manifest.

Observability expectations:
- Sidecars must emit telemetry at 30s intervals for heartbeat metrics and support a /metrics scrape.
- When error rates exceed thresholds, sidecar must capture a 30s diagnostic snapshot (bounded to 10MB) and make it retrievable by the control plane via a signed URL (only when permitted by confidentiality policy).

Manifest and Artifact Delivery
-----------------------------
- Model artifacts and sidecar config are delivered via a signed manifest (JSON) with fields: manifest_id, artifacts: [{name, sha256, url, size_bytes}], config: {runtime_flags, env_vars}, signature (ed25519).
- Sidecar verifies signature against a customer-provided public key or a Redwood-signed delegation certificate chain depending on deployment mode.
- Sidecars must support a local file repository mode (for air-gapped installs) where manifests are applied from a configured path; signature verification still required.

Example manifest (JSON snippet):
```json
{
  "manifest_id": "m-20260112-7f3a",
  "artifacts": [
    {"name": "model-v1.pt", "sha256": "...", "url": "https://artifacts.example/internal/m-.../model-v1.pt", "size_bytes": 734003200}
  ],
  "config": {"kv_cache_size": 512, "quantization_profile": "q4_0"},
  "signature": "...ed25519..."
}
```

Configuration Table (mandatory keys)
- manifest_verify: true|false
- artifact_store: https|file
- metrics_port: integer
- otlp_endpoint: host:port or empty
- tls_mode: mTLS|required
- retention.prompts_seconds: integer (0 means no persistence)

Example YAML sidecar configuration:
```yaml
manifest_verify: true
artifact_store: file
artifact_local_path: /var/redwood/artifacts
metrics_port: 9100\notlp_endpoint: 127.0.0.1:4317\ntls_mode: mTLS\nretention:
  prompts_seconds: 30
```

Security and Compliance Requirements
------------------------------------
- Keys and secrets: sidecar must support integration with customer KMS or an HSM. Private deployments default to customer-managed keys.
- No plaintext prompt storage: any local caching must be encrypted at rest with keys the customer controls. Default retention is 30s.
- Audit logs: sidecar must produce signed, append-only audit events for manifest apply, control operations, and admin reads. These logs must be exportable to the customer's SIEM.
- Image and manifest signing: all sidecar images and manifests must be signed and verified before execution.

Testing, Validation, and Release Process
---------------------------------------
Acceptance tests for every sidecar release (minimal):
1. Manifest verification flow (valid, tampered, missing signature).
2. Control API auth (expired certs, wrong tenant).
3. Load test: p95 latency at defined model sizes and hardware classes.
4. Telemetry emission and trace correlation test.
5. Security: KMS/HSM integration and local key rotation test.

Canary and rollout strategy:
1. Canary on 1 customer environment with automatic rollback on errors >0.5% 5xx for 15m.
2. Gradual rollout following the canary plan: 5%, 20%, 50%, 100% with 30m observation windows.

Migration and Compatibility Notes
--------------------------------
- Backward compatibility: older sidecars must accept the new /control endpoints but should return HTTP 501 for operations they cannot perform.
- A compatibility shim is provided that translates legacy manifest formats into the new signed manifest schema for up to 12 months after rollout.
- Customers on heavily regulated air-gapped deployments will be migrated with a special opt-in path requiring on-site validation and extended support.

Operational Runbook (short)
---------------------------
1. If /healthz reports ready=false, check model_state and logs. If model_state == "loading" for >5m, check artifact integrity (sha256) and available memory.
2. If telemetry shows rising error rate >0.5% 5xx: trigger canary rollback (control plane) and collect diagnostic snapshot.
3. For failed manifest apply: instruct sidecar to rollback to last-good manifest (POST /control/activate with last_good_manifest_id).

Consequences and Alternatives Considered
---------------------------------------
Consequences:
- Pros: consistent operational surface, easier debugging, clearer security posture, and predictable SLOs.
- Cons: increased sidecar complexity, slight latency overhead for control-plane ops.

Alternatives considered:
1. Keep ad-hoc sidecars per customer: rejected due to fragmentation and support burden.
2. Full remote-managed runtime (no sidecars): rejected because customer network/air-gap and key management requirements prevent it.
3. Heavyweight orchestration agent with expanded responsibilities (e.g., direct model execution): rejected for scope creep and security risk.

Owners and Governance
---------------------
Owner: Runtime Platform team (runtime-ops@redwood.com)
Approval: Director of Infrastructure and Head of Security
Review cadence: annual or on major private-deployment feature launches.

Related Docs
------------
- Private deployment overview: /confluence/eng-private-deployments/deployment-guides/private-deployments-overview
- Runtime manifest signing spec: /confluence/architecture-and-standards/model-serving-standards/model-artifact-provenance-and-signing-standard-2026.json

Appendix: Example error envelope
-------------------------------
```json
{ "code": "MODEL_LOAD_FAILURE", "message": "artifact checksum mismatch", "retriable": false }
```

If questions arise about interoperability, contact runtime-ops@redwood.com.
